reasons: No tests or other proof of correctness are visible in the packet.
Only one breaker and one control house shape are handled, and every other schedule item passes through unchanged.
Sizes and gaps are display choices, so their usefulness depends on the stated limits being understood by viewers.
Identifier renaming must stay in step with every reference list, and only four lists are visibly updated.

terms.meaning: a row or group in the project timetable that says what is installed and when.
a collection of facts taken from source documents, each with a note on how far it can be trusted.
a short label that says where a value came from and why it can be used.
a link from a part's size to the specific source fact that set it.
safe to run twice: the second run gives the same result as the first.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and imports
sections.what: States the purpose of the file: refine schedule scopes into shared solids, with unresolved quantities never creating installed items. It limits the first slice to one representative breaker and one control house.
sections.why: Likely reason: the header states the limit so reviewers do not expect a full inventory.
sections.watch_out: Only the breaker and control house are changed, so every other schedule item passes through unchanged.

sections.name: _provenance
sections.title: Source label builder
sections.what: Builds a short label that states where a value came from and why it is used. The source is always the same bounded assembly library.
sections.why: Likely reason: every displayed value carries a visible reason, so schematic values are not mistaken for surveyed data.
sections.watch_out: The source name is fixed, so a label cannot name a real vendor or document.

sections.name: _part
sections.title: Building one display solid
sections.what: Creates one box or cylinder with a name, size, position, material and provenance labels. The labels mark the shape as typical or rule-based, and two notes describe its limits.
sections.why: Likely reason: every part carries its disclaimers so the schematic status is never lost.
sections.watch_out: Every part gets the same timing limitation, so no single part can show its own construction date.

sections.name: _breaker
sections.title: Representative breaker parts
sections.what: Lists the parts of one representative circuit breaker: a foundation, two supports, a tank and six bushings arranged as three phases with two sides each.
sections.why: Likely reason: a simple fixed model gives a recognisable breaker without any vendor drawing.
sections.watch_out: The breaker shape is fixed in code, so real breaker dimensions would have to be added here.

sections.name: _house_bindings
sections.title: Binding plan dimensions to evidence
sections.what: Copies the stated long-axis and short-axis plan dimensions onto the house floor and walls they control. It then reconciles the claims and keeps only those allowed for model use.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a stated plan dimension set the house size without treating it as a surveyed measurement.
sections.watch_out: A budget of 40,000 records is enforced, and going over it stops the process with an error.

sections.name: _house (part 1)
sections.title: Sizing the control house
sections.what: Sets the house length and width from an eligible plan dimension when one exists, and otherwise uses 12 by 6 metres. It then builds the floor, roof and four walls, and rejects sizes outside 1 to 500 metres.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fallback size keeps the house visible even when no plan dimension is supplied.
sections.watch_out: A size outside 1 to 500 metres raises an error rather than being drawn, so a unit mistake in the plan stops the whole refinement.

sections.name: _house (part 2)
sections.title: Attaching sources to house parts
sections.what: Links each part's length and width to the source fact that sets it, when such a fact exists. It marks the geometry as inferred and returns the parts with an overall height of 4 metres.
sections.why: Likely reason: records exactly which source fact sized each part, so the origin can be checked later.
sections.watch_out: Height and wall thickness are not linked to any source, so the house height is always the schematic value.

sections.name: refine_package_assemblies (part 1)
sections.title: Renaming install scopes to shared assemblies
sections.what: Copies the model, rebinds the house evidence and rebuilds the review list for package claims. It then renames each onsite control house or breaker installation row into one representative assembly with quantity one.
sections.why: Likely reason: a schedule row that says install breaker should become one representative breaker, not a counted inventory.
sections.watch_out: Only items where every supporting activity matches the phrase are renamed, so mixed activity lists are left alone.

sections.name: refine_package_assemblies (part 2)
sections.title: Building parts and fixing links after renaming
sections.what: Gives each renamed item its parts and envelope size. It moves the control house away from the breakers if they are too close, then updates every reference list to the new identifiers.
sections.why: Likely reason: the house needs a clear access gap beside the equipment, and renames must not break links elsewhere in the model.
sections.watch_out: The 6 metre gap is only a display spacing, not an engineering clearance, and any reference list left behind will point at a deleted identifier.

sections.name: refine_package_assemblies (part 3)
sections.title: Adding the limitation note and returning a checked copy
sections.what: Adds a fixed limitation note to the model once, then returns a fresh copy that has passed model validation.
sections.why: Likely reason: the note tells viewers this is a slice and not a full inventory, and validation catches bad data early.
sections.watch_out: The duplicate check compares exact text, so any edit to the note will add a second copy beside the old one.

summary: Replaces the schedule's breaker and control house installation rows with one representative drawn assembly each, without counting real inventory.
purpose: Turns a schedule's breaker and control house installation rows into one representative assembly each, so the 3D view has a recognisable object. The file never adds real installed quantities.
why: Likely reason: the app needs drawable shapes for these items, but the source data does not support real counts or geometry, so each item gets one clearly labelled stand-in.
how: 1. Check that the evidence bundle belongs to the same project as the model. 2. Copy the model so the original is untouched. 3. Attach any plan dimensions from the evidence to the house parts. 4. Rebuild the review items for claims that are not eligible for model use. 5. Rename each matching schedule component to a breaker or control house assembly with quantity one. 6. Build the parts and overall size for each renamed item. 7. Move the house away from the breaker if they are too close. 8. Update every reference list to the new identifiers. 9. Add the standing limitation note and return a validated copy.
inputs: A project model with schedule components and activities, and an evidence bundle for the same project.
outputs: A new project model copy in which matching schedule items are renamed as breaker or control house assemblies, with parts, sizes, positions and limitation notes, and with review items refreshed.
risks: Renaming changes identifiers, so any saved link or code that uses the old identifiers breaks unless every reference is updated. Display sizes can look like real measurements, and the house size comes from plan evidence only after eligibility checks.
debug: Start with the refine function and check that the schedule activity names match the install phrases exactly. If the house moves unexpectedly, check the breaker positions and the 6 metre gap. If a plan error appears, check the long-axis and short-axis evidence records and confirm their values are plain numbers between 1 and 500 metres. If a claim budget error appears, the evidence bundle is too large for one run.
